modules.title: Module 1: Python for Data Analysis

points: ndarrays store one data type in contiguous memory
Vectorised operations replace slow Python loops
Broadcasting combines arrays of different shapes
lessons.recap: Think in arrays and let NumPy do the looping in C.

lessons.title: 1.3 Pandas DataFrames: Clean, Group & Summarise
lessons.summary: Load a CSV, fix messy values and answer business questions in a few lines.

fillna and astype repair missing or mistyped data

quiz.q: Which Pandas method replaces missing values?

quiz.a: Combine arrays of different but compatible shapes

modules.title: Module 2: Machine Learning Foundations
modules.description: Train, evaluate and improve your first predictive models with scikit-learn.

lessons.title: 2.1 Supervised Learning & Train/Test Splits
lessons.summary: How models learn from labelled examples, and how to measure them honestly.
points: Features (X) predict a target (y)
Hold out a test set the model never sees
Overfitting means great training scores but poor test scores
lessons.recap: Never grade a model on the data it trained on.

lessons.title: 2.2 Regression & Classification with scikit-learn
lessons.summary: Two model families that solve most everyday prediction problems.
points: Regression predicts numbers such as price
Classification predicts labels such as churn
Every estimator shares fit, predict and score
lessons.recap: Pick the family from the question: a number or a category?

lessons.title: 2.3 Model Evaluation: Accuracy, Precision & Recall
lessons.summary: Choosing the metric that matches the business cost of mistakes.
points: Accuracy misleads on imbalanced data
Precision asks: of my positives, how many were right?
Recall asks: of the real positives, how many did I find?

example.label: Pick the metric
lines: Spam filter → precision (don't hide real mail)
Disease screening → recall (don't miss a case)

lessons.recap: The right metric is the one that reflects the real cost of an error.

quiz.q: Why do we keep a separate test set?
quiz.a: To measure performance on data the model never saw
wrong: To store backups of the data
